packages.label: שֵׁם וְנֶפֶשׁ וּמְפֻרְסָם
packages.reason: The Rebbe explicitly equates all three as a single conceptual identity: the Name (שֵׁם) of a person IS their Soul (נֶפֶשׁ) and IS their Renown (מְפֻרְסָם). They are not cause-and-effect; they are three parallel dimensions of the same existential reality — the essential being and presence of a person (specifically the Tzaddik) in the world. Surrendering one's שֵׁם is therefore, by identity, surrendering one's נֶפֶשׁ, which is מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ in the fullest sense. The Torah teaches the positive path: the holy leader willingly gives up his reputation (his שֵׁם/מְפֻרְסָם = his נֶפֶשׁ) to achieve divine unity (יִחוּד), thereby saving Israel.
